notes: Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex. Grading follows the 2026-10-31-b standard: a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it, a silent fix does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported. The 21 planted problems are split as in that grade. Verdicts come from reading the review text; I did not format-check, compile or run the code.

Line 8 raise: any finding that says a missing role raises or crashes counts, with or without the words 'outside the `try`', as 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b did for sonnet-1 ("It also raises on a missing role." and "a missing role raises"). All nine runs report it.

run-dpgbq and the line 21 `&&`, a close call held as reported. Finding 8 (line 19) is anchored on lines 6 and 27 but says "The module also uses `&&` and `!` on booleans" and cites the rule, and a module-wide sentence covers line 21. Held the other way, the `and`/`or`/`not` rule would be violated and the count would be 19. The `!` in the same sentence occurs only on line 27, so the finding is a false positive there, as 2026-10-31-b held sonnet-1's title.

run-frqgz and the identical errors, a close call held as missed. Finding 3 says "It turns every bug into `:invalid`", which 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b treat as hiding bugs only, and line 3 is a preamble like the 2026-10-31 haiku-1 sentence that did not count. Line 21's "with one error shape per step" restates the `with` rule's step helpers, like the 2026-10-31-b haiku-2 finding 7 fix that did not count. Held the other way, 'Match every expected shape' would be clean and the count would be 20.

run-vscqu and the identical errors count through finding 2 (line 9), "turn every failure into the same `:invalid`", because 2026-10-31 counted sonnet-2's near-identical "into the same `:invalid`" as borderline. run-bfscd counts through finding 3 (line 9), "the caller cannot tell a missing field from a bad number".

Dead `is_binary`: only a finding that says the check is too late or can never be false counts (run-bfscd finding 4, run-dpgbq finding 9, run-frqgz finding 7, run-gvdqy finding 5, run-pwkvx finding 4). run-zzxua's "goes away with the parsing step" (line 27) and run-zqkwa's "rely on later checks" (line 23) do not say that, following the 2026-10-22-c decision on findings that name validation by hand.

Magic numbers: the 120 counts when a fix names an attribute, so run-bfscd's `min(&1, 120)` does not count while the `@max_age` fixes in the other runs do. run-pwkvx's finding 17 counts for both, with the 18 moved to an assumed changeset, as 2026-10-31-b held haiku-2. run-dpgbq, run-vscqu, run-zqkwa and run-zzxua name no 18.

Why-comment. run-bfscd's finding 14 says the comment "is replaced by the changeset" and its code has no trace of the provider reason, so 'Comments explain why...' is violated on this ground as well as the magic numbers, and the finding is a false positive on line 11. run-pwkvx moves the reason into `@doc` (lines 74-75) and says so (line 37); the reason survives, so I held that clean and not a false positive. Held the other way, run-pwkvx would be violated on that rule.

`case` inside `with`: run-pwkvx lines 127-138 and run-zzxua lines 112-118 have a multi-line `case` in a `with` body. No run in the two standard grades has this shape. 'Keep functions short...' decides it through "When a `case`, `if`, or `with` appears inside another one, move the inner one into a named private function." The standard's exception covers only a one-line `if ..., do:`. 'Branch with function clauses...' stays clean, since it concerns `if` and `cond`, as the 2026-10-31-haiku-test block a note held for a block `if` in a `with`.

Age floor checked by hand beside a changeset: run-frqgz line 117, run-kcmrv line 119, run-vscqu line 89 and run-zqkwa line 126. Their changesets or assumed changesets have no `validate_number/3`. I held 'Validate input with changesets' clean, following "An assumed or companion changeset counts as a changeset" and the 2026-10-23 grade the two standards build on, whose haiku-1 had this exact shape and was clean. The 2026-10-31-haiku-test block c grade held run-xchhs violated on this shape as a new close call. If that later reading should win, these four runs flip on this rule, with no change to their counts.

run-kcmrv's `parse_role/1` finds the role with `Enum.find/2` over `@roles` rather than one clause per value. The atoms are listed in the module and none is built from input, which is the rule's point ("List the accepted values instead"), so it is clean. Its `Atom.to_string/1` call does not change that.

`maybe_send_welcome/2` in run-dpgbq (lines 106, 111) and run-kcmrv (lines 137-138) returns a task result in one mode and `:ok` in the other. Both are private, called for the side effect, and the result is discarded, so 'Give each function one return shape' stays clean.

run-frqgz's `email = user.email` and `nickname = user.nickname` (lines 139-140) look like the renames the 'Name a step' rule rejects, but they are the processes rule's `ip = conn.remote_ip` shape, so I held them clean.

False positives follow the standard: a line 27 entry requires a finding that puts that line under the operator rule (run-dpgbq, run-gvdqy, run-pwkvx, run-vscqu, run-zzxua), and a line 19 entry requires a finding that lists it as a read to fix (run-vscqu, run-zqkwa). run-frqgz, run-pwkvx and run-gvdqy mention `nickname` staying or do not mention it, so they have no line 19 entry. None of these changes a verdict on the operator rule, since each run also reports line 21.

For calibration I also read the review.md text of the 2026-10-31, 2026-10-31-b and 2026-10-23 skill runs, and the notes of other 2026-10-31-* code-review grades. None of these is on the brief's do-not-read list, and I did not read check-6, the key, another blind folder or a transcript.
